concerns.text: The normal-force confound flagged at the prior stage remains unaddressed. In the sliding regime, hand torque is dominated by Coulomb friction (τ ≈ μ·N·r), so k_est = |Δτ|/|Δv| will track contact load and friction, not stiffness. The spec's Assumptions assert the proxy is valid 'in the sliding regime' but offers no control for, or measurement of, normal force N. Construct validity of the entire 'Virtual Tactile' mechanism is broken unless FR-001 is revised (e.g., normalize by estimated normal force, or reframe k_est explicitly as a friction/resistance proxy rather than stiffness).

The 'zero-shot' claim is not supported by the design. The spec randomizes friction 0.1–1.2 for novel objects (Methodology/US-1) and tests at 0.8–1.2, but never defines the training friction distribution or a mechanism guaranteeing test objects lie outside it. If training and test friction ranges overlap, 'unseen damping conditions' is false and SC-001 measures in-distribution robustness, not zero-shot adaptation. The spec must define the training distribution and require test friction values strictly outside it (or rename the claim).

Thresholds k_est > 1.0 and k_est < 0.2 are dimensionally meaningless: k_est = |Δτ|/|Δv| carries units (N·m·s/m) whose magnitude depends on joint and object scales. A fixed numeric cutoff cannot generalize across objects/geometries. The spec should require a normalized or per-object-calibrated k_est before threshold-based reward scaling, or define the thresholds relative to a reference distribution.

A paired t-test on binary success-rate outcomes across ~10 novel objects is statistically mismatched: per-object success rates are proportions from few episodes, the pairing unit is ill-defined (episodes vs objects), and n≈10 gives negligible power for a 15% effect. Use a mixed-effects logistic regression or paired test on per-object proportions with an arcsine/logit transform and a power analysis; the Assumption that n is 'sufficient' is asserted, not justified.

US-2's validation test checks that k_est 'correlates linearly with the ground-truth friction coefficient' — but the spec elsewhere calls k_est a stiffness proxy. If the ground truth for validation is friction while the construct is stiffness, the validation target and the construct are mismatched; if k_est is actually a friction proxy, FR-002's 'stiffness' framing and reward-scaling rationale must be restated. Pick one construct and validate against its matching ground truth.
